title: DFS Through Stockholm: Follow the Dead-Ends!
description: Watch DFS carve a route across real street-map intersections in Stockholm’s Södermalm. This visualization shows how DFS explores deeply before backtracking to find an available path.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ DFS is a “go-deep-first” graph search that explores one path to the max depth before backtracking—perfect for seeing why depth-first strategies can leap into dead-ends.

🗺️ In real street-map terms, we model intersections as **nodes** and roads as **edges** (often with direction/weight rules depending on your graph build). DFS then performs a recursive/stack-based traversal, marking visited nodes to avoid infinite loops, producing a traversal tree that reflects the neighborhood’s connectivity in Södermalm.

🔍 Key technical takeaway: DFS finds *a* path (not guaranteed shortest), and the order depends on how neighbors are sorted (e.g., by angle, distance, or edge ID).
